text.p: Colombian Transport Minister Carlos Hernan Lopez resigned on Sunday just hours after the attorney general ordered him suspended for three months on suspicion of abusing his position.
Lopez told an evening news conference he was stepping down in order "not to get in the way of the official investigation."
There was no immediate word on who President Ernesto Samper might name as a successor to Lopez, who was a cabinet member despite being a member of the opposition Conservative Party.

Lopez was the subject of a censure motion brought before Congress last week in which mainstream members of the Conservative Party accused him of appearing publicly to promote the party's dissident wing.
Lopez was also accused of using an official helicopter to ferry political cronies to rallies. Colombia's constitution forbids government ministers from involvement in partisan activities.
Lopez emerged unscathed from the censure motion but was sanctioned on Sunday by Attorney General Jaime Bernal, who opened a formal investigation into the allegations against him.
